parsed.reason: Every specific is backed by research_notes: short-term safety, the one-to-two-month definition (UC Davis), the November 2025 AHA abstract with 4.6% vs 2.7% over five years, its preliminary and non-causal status, the poor-sleep explanation, grogginess at higher doses, and fracture caution for older adults. It does present one-to-two months as settled when GoodRx says a week or two. 'Higher doses' also loosely broadens the controlled-release, over-3mg detail. Neither rises to a wrong fact. It gives no dosing regimen and ends with a doctor pointer for long-term use, which is good safety handling. The tone is casual enough, but the stats and caveats make it read more like a summarized article than a quick friend's text.
